Tesla Rolls Out FSD V14.3 Lite to Legacy Model S and Model X With Intel MCU for the First Time
6 photos
Photo: @LeonardCampagna via X
Tesla launched a "Lite" variant of FSD V14 for HW3 vehicles in June, but only on Model 3 and Model Y vehicles. The Model S and Model X were left behind, but that is now changing. Tesla confirmed that the FSD V14.3 Lite is rolling out to legacy Model S and Model X equipped with Intel processors. Vehicles that combine HW3 with MCU3 (Ryzen) will likely follow shortly.
Tesla FSD development hit a snag on HW3 vehicles when the ever-increasing hardware requirements could no longer be met by older hardware. Tesla promised to address the situation, but the process took more than two years. Until recently, Teslas equipped with HW3 Autopilot computers were stuck on FSD V12 because newer builds could not run on their outdated computers.
Things changed for the better in June, when Model 3 and Model Y equipped with HW3 processors got a "Lite" variant of the FSD V14. As Tesla explained at the time, this was a distilled variant of the FSD V14 software that runs on HW4 vehicles. This introduced some limitations , including a longer reaction time that could affect safety in unpredictable ways. However, it was a step up from the old V12 builds.
While Model 3 and Model Y owners were already finding the limits of the new FSD V14 Lite software, Model S and Model X owners could only dream. Hopes got a boost in September, when Tesla began to test FSD V14 Lite on Model S and Model X. However, the tests were limited to early access (Wave1) testers, and we've seen no further evidence that Tesla was advancing with FSD V14 Lite on Model S/X. Until now, that is.
The carmaker confirmed that FSD V14 Lite starts rolling out to Model S and Model X vehicles equipped with an Intel MCU. These are considered "legacy" vehicles, some built in 2017 or even earlier. That's because Tesla offered a MCU2 retrofit to MCU1 vehicles for a cool $2,500. Those who also paid FSD in full got a free HW2/HW2.5 to HW3 upgrade, thus making their vehicles eligible to run FSD V14.3 Lite in the latest software update.
The same update (2026.38.5.1) also includes the Halloween update, FSD V14.3.12, and the Automatic Collision Evasion feature. Still, they are irrelevant to legacy HW3 Model S/X vehicles. Halloween Update is currently supported on Ryzen processors only, while FSD V14.3.12 and ACE are HW4-exclusive.
So far, HW3-equipped Model S/X with Ryzen MCUs haven't gotten the latest FSD V14.3 Lite update, but that is likely to change shortly. Select AMD-based HW3 Model S/X vehicles have received previous FSD V14 Lite builds. However, the rollout has been very limited, probably because Tesla was still testing it.
Based on the experience of Model 3/Y owners who received FSD V14 Lite, the automated driving software puts a lot of strain on the HW3 computers. This can lead to overheating and the familiar "red hands" error. A thorough cleaning of the cooling radiators is advised before testing FSD on older vehicles.
